lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Rewrite grab it, put that in, and do the next thing so a robot can pack one eraser and one sharpener into the pencil case. What four precise steps replace those vague lines?

FEEDBACK
The repair names the eraser and the sharpener, and each object is picked up and then placed in the case. Step 1: pick up the eraser. Step 2: place the eraser in the pencil case. Step 3: pick up the sharpener. Step 4: place the sharpener in the pencil case. Put it in is still too vague, because the robot is not told which object moves or where it goes.

WATCH FOR
A common mistake is to write put it in and expect a robot to know which object and which container were meant. A precise instruction names the verb, the object and the place.

teaching.model: A paper robot needs a precise verb and a named object in every step, because a missing object is unclear. Put it in fails: it does not name the object, and in does not name the place. Work on paper. No computer is required. Now choose a different example to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same technology idea on a new place, person, source or context, not a copy of the worked example. Review accuracy of evidence.
teaching.why: This helps the learner base claims on observation, fair tests and design evidence, rather than guessing from a picture alone. Keep every claim linked to what was seen, measured or tested against criteria.

visuals.alt: Put it in names neither the object nor the place. Place the pencil in the case names both.
visuals.teaches: A paper robot needs a precise verb and a named object in every step.

visuals.alt: Pick up the ruler names the object. Place the ruler in the case names the object and the place.
visuals.teaches: Precise packing steps say which object moves and where that object goes.
